I read the whole target file (two theorems) and the supporting declarations in TwinPerpV3A6ModelBasic.lean: evalCodes_mem_omegaT, cPerms_mem, aeWord_mem_omegaT and curtisPerms_mem. I also grepped for c3Perms and c1iPerms.

The only repeated proof text is the "this permutation lies in omegaT" step. It appears in ae6ModelC3_proved at lines 28-30, in ae6ModelC1_inv_proved at lines 52-57, and in cPerms_mem in the Basic file. Each copy is a List.mem_map destructuring followed by evalCodes_mem_omegaT. The C1 copy adds a getD/getElem? case split for the default element. Each copy is two to six lines of routine unfolding over an existing lemma, and the two uses have different list shapes (map over the list versus getD at an index). A shared lemma would be a thin wrapper around existing API, which the rubric excludes.

The remaining steps differ in substance. The first theorem unpacks a Schreier-table certificate and compares tables. The second proves an iSup-over-conjugates equality from per-generator memberships. I found no nontrivial reasoning duplicated across the two proofs.
